$comment: SAMPLE BRAND (invented). Every field filled in, to show what a finished brand message looks like.

positioning.audience: Busy neighbours on the north side who want real bread but can't get to a bakery before work.
positioning.oneSentence: A neighbourhood sourdough bakery that opens at 6:30 so good bread fits a working morning.
positioning.oneParagraph: Rye & Rise bakes slow-fermented sourdough, rye and seasonal buns every night and opens at 6:30 on weekdays. Pre-order by 9 pm and your loaf waits on a named shelf, so the walk to work includes breakfast.
positioning.differentFrom: Supermarket bread (fast, soft, forgettable) and weekend-only artisan bakeries.

oneLiner.problem: Most people only get proper bread at weekends.
oneLiner.solution: Rye & Rise opens at 6:30 with tonight's sourdough on a shelf with your name on it,
oneLiner.result: so every weekday starts with a real breakfast.

character.who: Commuters and young families on the north side
character.want: Good bread on a weekday without planning their morning around it

problem.external: Bakeries open too late and sell out early
problem.internal: They feel they settle for second-best food on weekdays
problem.philosophical: Good bread shouldn't be a weekend luxury

guide.empathy: We bake at night because we have early mornings too.

steps: Pick up from your named shelf from 6:30
plan.promise: If your loaf isn't right, the next one is free.

failure: Another rushed breakfast of supermarket toast
success: Warm bread on the table before the school run
A five-minute stop that feels like a treat

transformation.to: Fed well and a little ahead of the day

clients: Supplies the breakfast club at a local primary school
